tier_reason: Third-party harness is public (Makefile, docker-compose.yml, configs/*) with pinned prebuilt images, but it is a 0-star archived personal repo, not a well-known suite; the chart footer gives only '24 cores, 29.0 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS' with no CPU model, no compiler flags exist for either side, the P99 figures appear only as approximate README prose (the chart shows means only, raw results are not committed), and the 'HTTPS/1.1' scenario actually negotiates HTTP/2. Tier C stands.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README Key Findings (approximate best-per-scenario values, 0% errors for all four proxies at 5,000 req/s): HTTPS/1.1 Traefik best mean about 0.48 ms and best P99 about 1.47 ms, Nginx P99 about 24 ms; HTTPS/2 Traefik best mean about 0.46 ms and P99 about 1.37 ms, HAProxy next at about 1.79 ms P99. Plain HTTP/1.1: all four within about 5%, Caddy/HAProxy best mean (about 0.41 ms), HAProxy best P99 (about 1.09 ms), so no Traefik win. The only committed chart (assets/local-results/benchmark.png, generated 2026-04-10) shows mean latency and throughput only: unrestricted HTTPS means are all near or below about 2 ms; in the 2-core restricted run Nginx means are about 32 ms (HTTPS/1.1) and 34 ms (HTTPS/2) against about 1.3 ms for Traefik on HTTPS/1.1 (read from chart, approximate). Per-proxy P99 tables are not published. Note: the 'HTTPS/1.1' row is really HTTP/2 (vegeta -http2 defaults to true and the harness never passes -http2=false).
corrections.workload: Fixed-rate Vegeta v12.13.0 load of 5,000 req/s for 20 s (5 s warmup per proxy/protocol, shuffled run order) for GET /data.json (~20 KB static JSON served by an nginx 1.28.3 backend) through each proxy; load generator, proxies and backend share one Docker host. -connections=64 sets only Vegeta's max idle connections per host (MaxIdleConnsPerHost), not the connection count. Both TLS scenarios negotiate HTTP/2 via ALPN (vegeta's -http2 flag defaults to true; nginx listens 'ssl http2', HAProxy advertises 'alpn h2,http/1.1', Go servers advertise h2), so requests are multiplexed over few TLS connections; the plain-HTTP scenario is HTTP/1.1. Run twice: unrestricted and restricted (cpus 2.0, mem_limit 4G per proxy via docker-compose.restricted.yml).
corrections.hardware: Chart footer: host with 24 cores, 29.0 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (CPU model not stated); all containers on the same host; optional restricted run limits each proxy to 2 CPUs (CFS quota) and 4 GB.
corrections.baseline: Nginx 1.28.3 (C, official nginx:1.28.3 image) and HAProxy 3.3.6 (C, official haproxy:3.3.6 image) in Docker. Configs read: nginx worker_processes auto, epoll, multi_accept, upstream keepalive 64, TLSv1.2/1.3 with ECDHE AES-GCM ciphers, no ssl_session_cache, proxy_buffers 8 4k; HAProxy maxconn 20000, no-tls-tickets, http-reuse always, alpn h2,http/1.1. All proxies use the same self-signed RSA-4096 certificate.
corrections.caveats: Benchmark repo (fabianwimberger/reverse-proxy-benchmark) is a third-party suite but a 0-star personal repo the owner archived on 2026-07-17; hardware lacks a CPU model and the proxies are prebuilt images with unknown build flags on both sides. Fixed-rate latency test at 5,000 req/s, not saturation throughput; all four proxies sustain the rate with 100% success, so differences are sub-millisecond except tails. Harness flaw: the 'HTTPS/1.1' scenario is actually HTTP/2 because vegeta's -http2 flag defaults to true (attack.go v12.13.0) and the harness only passes -insecure, so both TLS rows measure HTTP/2 over a few multiplexed connections; Nginx serves each connection from a single worker process, which plausibly explains its tail latency more than any language effect. The P99 values exist only as approximate README prose; the committed chart shows means only and raw vegeta JSON is not committed. Restricted-run asymmetry: nginx worker_processes auto counts the host's 24 CPUs under a 2-CPU CFS quota, whereas Traefik v3.6.13 (go.mod go 1.25.0) gets Go 1.25's container-aware GOMAXPROCS (likely cause of Nginx's ~32 ms restricted means; not tested). No HTTP/1.1 win: the author credits Nginx with plaintext throughput and calls HTTP/1.1 'extremely tight'. Not a same-algorithm comparison: different proxy designs and TLS stacks (Go crypto/tls vs OpenSSL).
corrections.why_faster: Not established by the benchmark (no profiling, no per-proxy tables). Different programs and TLS stacks (Go crypto/tls with assembly AES-GCM vs OpenSSL in Nginx/HAProxy). Probable harness factors rather than language: both TLS scenarios run HTTP/2 over few multiplexed connections, which Nginx pins to one worker process per connection while Go's net/http serves streams on goroutines across cores; in the restricted run Go 1.25 sizes GOMAXPROCS to the 2-CPU quota while nginx starts 24 workers.

notes: Numbers in the record match the README text; added that the 'HTTPS/1.1' scenario is really HTTP/2 (vegeta -http2 default true, verified in tsenart/vegeta v12.13.0 attack.go and lib/attack.go), that -connections=64 is only an idle-pool cap, and that the P99 figures are prose-only with no committed raw results. Record shortcomings: TLS rows mislabelled (both HTTP/2), single-host Docker run without CPU model, prebuilt images with unknown flags, restricted-run GOMAXPROCS/worker_processes asymmetry, no HTTP/1.1 win; not a language-level result (same_algorithm false). Traefik metadata checked: MIT, 65.2k stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-10-08 (active).
